title: Barrel House, the fish fry king, and tough parties at Belmont
summary: Nash and Allen discuss finding Barrel House's address; Nash calls him the fish fry king and describes how tough the crowds were at fish fries out at the Belmont place.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh, you told me you saw him, I guess in October you told me you saw him. Yeah, I did. I did see him, but I, you know, it's been common.
He died since then? You said you were going to find his address. I don't know. I don't believe he did though. He may not be there. Yeah, Barrel House, you know him, huh?
No, you told me about him. I want you to find his address for me and you say you're going to do it.

Okay, I will. I'm going to find out where Barrel House is there, I'm sure. There'll be something in it for you, you know. Yeah, I'm going to find him. Man, he's a fish fry king around there. When they had them old fish fries, all out in the Zellemont, the battlefield, everywhere. Barrel House is there with his gift card. Where? Out in Zellemont? Out there, I mean out here at this, what do you call this place? The Belmont place. That's why them guys used to be so tough out there. You'd get out there and play a party, you know. If they catch you talking to the girls while you had about fifteen or twenty of them to whip when you step outside. Them guys are tough.
